title: What Earth's horizon costs
summary: At the south pole Earth sits low on the horizon and ridges hide it. With direct links only, the base moves {{r:dte_loss}} less of the cargo that lands, and fewer than half of its urgent items arrive within the year. A relay in view a tenth of the time, or rovers allowed to drive out of Earth's sight, wins most of it back.
summary_plain: At the south pole Earth sits low on the horizon and ridges hide it. With direct links only, the base moves 68 % less of the cargo that lands, and fewer than half of its urgent items arrive within the year. A relay in view a tenth of the time, or rovers allowed to drive out of Earth's sight, wins most of it back.
notes: E21 round 2 (experiments/phase4/run_phase4.py --round r2, analysis experiments/phase4/analyse_e21.py fit --round r2): P2 base, marketplace, pads 1 km unless stated, no plume, 20 seeds per cell, start years 2028-2031. Delays are censored at the year's end and shown as the median over seeds; shares and tonnes are means. Wording by LEAD, 22 Oct 2026 (round 2 replaces the round-1 total-throughput headline with the lander/bulk split).

base_link.source: results/E21_fit_r2.json: throughput_bound/site_link_fraction_dte_any_part/BASE; x 100; share of 2028-2031 in which any part of Earth's disc is above the terrain horizon at the base, 2.5 m antenna
base_link.label: Time Earth is in view at the base

dte_wait.source: results/table_E21_cells_r2.csv, row stage = A, comms = dte, mix = supervised_strict, column blackout_wait_vehicle_h; rover time spent waiting for Earth in the year, direct links only, supervised rovers, strict policy (mean of 20 seeds)
dte_wait.label: Rover time spent waiting for Earth

landed_always.source: results/table_E21_cells_r2.csv, row stage = A, comms = always, mix = supervised_strict, column delivered_landed_t; cargo brought down by landers and delivered inside the year (not regolith, not returns), Earth always in view
landed_always.label: Lander cargo moved, Earth always in view

landed_dte.source: results/table_E21_cells_r2.csv, row stage = A, comms = dte, mix = supervised_strict, column delivered_landed_t; the same with direct-to-Earth links only
landed_dte.label: Lander cargo moved, direct links only

dte_loss.source: pct_change of landed_always and landed_dte (unrounded); neg
dte_loss.label: Lander cargo lost with direct links

done_always.source: results/table_E21_cells_r2.csv, row stage = A, comms = always, mix = supervised_strict, column prio1_completion_share; x 100; share of urgent (priority-1) items ready in the year that are delivered in the year, Earth always in view
done_always.label: Urgent items delivered, Earth in view

done_dte.source: results/table_E21_cells_r2.csv, row stage = A, comms = dte, mix = supervised_strict, column prio1_completion_share; x 100; the same with direct-to-Earth links only
done_dte.label: Urgent items delivered, direct links

isru_lost.source: results/E21_fit_r2.json: throughput_bound/lost_at_never_linked_t/mean; regolith feedstock bound for the ISRU plant, which never sees Earth, that is not delivered under direct links only (the demand model hauls about two hundred tonnes a year there)
isru_lost.label: Regolith for the oxygen plant lost

pads_one_t.source: results/table_E21_cells_r2.csv, row stage = A, comms = dte, mix = default, column delivered_landed_t; Phase 2 fleet, direct links only, pads 1 km from the base
pads_one_t.label: Lander cargo, pads a kilometre out

pads_half_t.source: results/table_E21_cells_r2.csv, row stage = C, comms = dte, mix = default, pad_standoff_km = 0.5, criterion = any_part, column delivered_landed_t; the same with the pads 0.5 km from the base
pads_half_t.label: Lander cargo, pads half a kilometre out

pads_three_t.source: results/table_E21_cells_r2.csv, row stage = C, comms = dte, mix = default, pad_standoff_km = 3.0, criterion = any_part, column delivered_landed_t; the same with the pads 3 km from the base: no seed moves any lander cargo
pads_three_t.label: Lander cargo, pads three kilometres out

relay_done.source: results/table_E21_cells_r2.csv, row stage = A, comms = dte+relay, p = 0.1, mix = supervised_strict, column prio1_completion_share; x 100; a relay satellite in view a tenth of the time, besides direct links
relay_done.label: Urgent items delivered, relay a tenth

relay_p90.source: results/table_E21_cells_r2.csv, row stage = A, comms = dte+relay, p = 0.1, mix = supervised_strict, column delay_prio1_p90_censored_h_median; hours within which nine in ten urgent items are delivered (items still waiting at the year's end count with their wait so far), median over 20 seeds
relay_p90.label: Typical urgent wait, relay a tenth

always_p90.source: results/table_E21_cells_r2.csv, row stage = A, comms = always, mix = supervised_strict, column delay_prio1_p90_censored_h_median; the same with Earth always in view
always_p90.label: Typical urgent wait, Earth in view

strategic_done.source: results/table_E21_cells_r2.csv, row stage = A, comms = dte, mix = supervised_strategic, column prio1_completion_share; x 100; direct links only; supervised rovers that may drive without a link (strategic policy)
strategic_done.label: Urgent items, rovers drive out of sight

strategic_landed.source: results/table_E21_cells_r2.csv, row stage = A, comms = dte, mix = supervised_strategic, column delivered_landed_t; the same policy: lander cargo delivered inside the year
strategic_landed.label: Lander cargo, rovers drive out of sight

avoid_done.source: results/table_E21_cells_r2.csv, row stage = A, comms = dte, mix = supervised_strategic+avoid, column prio1_completion_share; x 100; direct links only; the strategic policy with a look-ahead that avoids starting drives that would lose the link
avoid_done.label: Urgent items, cautious autonomy

rover_dp.source: results/table_E21_breakeven_delay_r2.csv, row option = +1 rover, column delta_p; x 100; relay coverage that gives the same urgent delay as one extra rover, at half coverage, strict policy (bootstrap over seeds, 2,000 draws)
rover_dp.label: Relay coverage worth one extra rover

strategic_dp.source: results/table_E21_breakeven_delay_r2.csv, row option = strategic step, column delta_p; x 100; relay coverage that gives the same urgent delay as the strategic policy, at half coverage
strategic_dp.label: Relay coverage worth the autonomy step

rover_dp_lo.source: results/table_E21_breakeven_delay_r2.csv, row option = +1 rover, column delta_p_ci95_lo; x 100; lower end of the 95 % bootstrap interval (2,000 draws), percentage points of relay coverage
rover_dp_lo.label: One extra rover, low end

rover_dp_hi.source: results/table_E21_breakeven_delay_r2.csv, row option = +1 rover, column delta_p_ci95_hi; x 100; upper end of the same interval
rover_dp_hi.label: One extra rover, high end

strategic_dp_lo.source: results/table_E21_breakeven_delay_r2.csv, row option = strategic step, column delta_p_ci95_lo; x 100; lower end of the 95 % bootstrap interval (2,000 draws), percentage points of relay coverage
strategic_dp_lo.label: Autonomy step, low end

strategic_dp_hi.source: results/table_E21_breakeven_delay_r2.csv, row option = strategic step, column delta_p_ci95_hi; x 100; upper end of the same interval
strategic_dp_hi.label: Autonomy step, high end

steps.title: Earth hangs on the horizon
steps.text: Seen from the south pole Earth never climbs high, and ridges hide it. From the base it is in view {{r:base_link}} of the time. A rover driven or supervised from Earth needs that link.
steps.visual: Earth low over the ridge; the terrain shadow marks where it is hidden.
steps.text_plain: Seen from the south pole Earth never climbs high, and ridges hide it. From the base it is in view 59 % of the time. A rover driven or supervised from Earth needs that link.
steps.visual_plain: Earth low over the ridge; the terrain shadow marks where it is hidden.

steps.title: Waiting for Earth
steps.text: With direct links only, rovers spend {{r:dte_wait}} a year parked, waiting for Earth to rise.
steps.visual: Rovers parked in the waiting colour while Earth is below the ridge.
steps.text_plain: With direct links only, rovers spend 972 rover-hours a year parked, waiting for Earth to rise.
steps.visual_plain: Rovers parked in the waiting colour while Earth is below the ridge.

steps.title: The cargo it costs
steps.text: Cargo that comes down on landers suffers most. With direct links only the base moves {{r:landed_dte}} of it instead of {{r:landed_always}}: {{r:dte_loss}} less. Only {{r:done_dte}} of urgent items arrive within the year, against {{r:done_always}} with Earth always in view.
steps.visual: The delivery counter of the year, with and without the horizon.
steps.text_plain: Cargo that comes down on landers suffers most. With direct links only the base moves 9 t per year of it instead of 29 t per year: 68 % less. Only 43 % of urgent items arrive within the year, against 96 % with Earth always in view.
steps.visual_plain: The delivery counter of the year, with and without the horizon.

steps.title: One site never sees Earth
steps.text: The plant that makes oxygen from regolith sits where Earth is never in view, so the {{r:isru_lost}} of regolith hauled to it never arrives. That is nearly all the regolith lost, but it is not why urgent cargo is late.
steps.visual: The ISRU site highlighted; its route drawn in the colour for no link.
steps.text_plain: The plant that makes oxygen from regolith sits where Earth is never in view, so the 204 t per year of regolith hauled to it never arrives. That is nearly all the regolith lost, but it is not why urgent cargo is late.
steps.visual_plain: The ISRU site highlighted; its route drawn in the colour for no link.

steps.title: Where the pads sit decides it
steps.text: Take the base's usual mixed fleet. Landing pads half a kilometre from the base see Earth about as often as the base does, and lander cargo comes back to {{r:pads_half_t}}. At a kilometre it is {{r:pads_one_t}}. At three kilometres, where ridges hide Earth from the pads most of the time, it is {{r:pads_three_t}}: no lander cargo moves at all.
steps.visual: The two pads highlighted; legs from them drawn in the colour for no link.
steps.title_plain: Where the pads sit decides it
steps.text_plain: Take the base's usual mixed fleet. Landing pads half a kilometre from the base see Earth about as often as the base does, and lander cargo comes back to 23 t per year. At a kilometre it is 10 t per year. At three kilometres, where ridges hide Earth from the pads most of the time, it is 0 t per year: no lander cargo moves at all.
steps.visual_plain: The two pads highlighted; legs from them drawn in the colour for no link.

steps.title: A relay brings the cargo back, not the speed
steps.text: A relay satellite in view only a tenth of the time brings urgent deliveries back to {{r:relay_done}}. But in a typical year nine in ten urgent items arrive only within {{r:relay_p90}}, against {{r:always_p90}} with Earth always in view, and waits shrink slowly as the relay is in view more.
steps.visual: The base with a relay in view part of the time: rovers wait in the waiting colour between passes.
steps.title_plain: A relay brings the cargo back, not the speed
steps.text_plain: A relay satellite in view only a tenth of the time brings urgent deliveries back to 95 %. But in a typical year nine in ten urgent items arrive only within 134 h, against 9 h with Earth always in view, and waits shrink slowly as the relay is in view more.
steps.visual_plain: The base with a relay in view part of the time: rovers wait in the waiting colour between passes.

steps.title: Or let rovers drive out of sight
steps.text: With no relay at all, supervised rovers allowed to drive on their own out of Earth's sight deliver {{r:strategic_done}} of urgent items and {{r:strategic_landed}} of lander cargo. A cautious version that never starts a drive it cannot finish in sight gets only {{r:avoid_done}}: the cargo is where Earth cannot see.
steps.visual: Supervised rovers driving on through the stretch where the link is lost.
steps.title_plain: Or let rovers drive out of sight
steps.text_plain: With no relay at all, supervised rovers allowed to drive on their own out of Earth's sight deliver 89 % of urgent items and 26 t per year of lander cargo. A cautious version that never starts a drive it cannot finish in sight gets only 50 %: the cargo is where Earth cannot see.
steps.visual_plain: Supervised rovers driving on through the stretch where the link is lost.

steps.title: A rover or autonomy: too close to call
steps.text: With a relay in view half the time, one more rover is worth {{r:rover_dp}} (likely between {{r:rover_dp_lo}} and {{r:rover_dp_hi}}) and the autonomy step {{r:strategic_dp}} (likely between {{r:strategic_dp_lo}} and {{r:strategic_dp_hi}}). The ranges overlap widely, so this model cannot rank them.
steps.visual: A dot for each option, one extra rover and the autonomy step, with a line across its likely range.
steps.title_plain: A rover or autonomy: too close to call
steps.text_plain: With a relay in view half the time, one more rover is worth 12 percentage points of relay coverage (likely between 1 and 42) and the autonomy step 17 percentage points of relay coverage (likely between 11 and 40). The ranges overlap widely, so this model cannot rank them.
steps.visual_plain: A dot for each option, one extra rover and the autonomy step, with a line across its likely range.
